source: Cheshbon ha-nefesh, the accounting of the soul, is the tradition of taking stock in Elul, the month before Rosh Hashanah. These are the same questions asked of a bank balance, written by the owner for coaching sessions.
confidenceNote: Questions, not figures. The page stores your answers and nothing else; it computes nothing from them.
plain: Elul is the month before the new year, when Jews take stock. This page does the same for money, in your words, once a year. The answers are yours; nothing here scores them. There is also a shorter one for the new moon each month.

yearly.q: What did I give away this year, and did it match what I said I would?
yearly.hint: The Tzedakah page has the number. The question is about the gap, and how it feels.

yearly.q: What did I receive that I did not earn: a gift, a loan, help, a place to stay?
yearly.hint: Chosen family runs on this. Name it so it can be returned or passed on.

yearly.q: Who do I owe, in money or in kind, and have I said so out loud?
yearly.hint: A gemach, a friend, a parent, a fund. The debt that is unspoken costs the most.

yearly.q: If I had been hit by a bus in Av, would the right people have been in charge?
yearly.hint: The Chosen Family page lists the papers. Which ones are still not done?

yearly.q: Where did I spend to cover shame, and where did I not spend out of shame?
yearly.hint: A dinner you paid for to belong; care you put off because you did not feel you deserved it.

yearly.q: What money passed between me and my family of origin, and what did it cost?
yearly.hint: Strings, silence, a name not used. Or nothing, and that was fine. Write it down either way.

yearly.q: Did I rest from money one day a week, or did it follow me?
yearly.hint: No banking app on Shabbat is a practice. So is one no-spend day for those who do not keep it.

yearly.q: What is the one money thing I want to be true by next Elul?
yearly.hint: One. The pages here will hold the number; this is the sentence.

monthly.q: What did this month cost that I did not plan?
What is on the Jewish calendar in the next thirty days, and is it paid for?
Did I give this month? To whom?
Is there help I should ask for before next month?
